sections.h2: What to weigh before a quick sale in Bedford
sections.html:
Bedford is a small suburb in northeast Tarrant County with almost no vacant land left, so a house here competes in a crowded metro market. Sellers handle paperwork with Tarrant Appraisal District, a city rental registry and buyers who commute across the Metroplex. SH-121 runs through town, about 14 miles from downtown Fort Worth and 22 from downtown Dallas, and DFW International Airport is within five miles.

An estimated 47,958 people lived in Bedford in mid-2025, a 4.0% decline from the April 2020 base. About half of homes are rented, so one seller may be juggling tenants, a registration file and a tax ceiling transfer at the same moment.

A midpoint owner-occupied home is worth $350,700, and owners occupy 50.6% of units. Renters pay $1,502 a month at the midpoint.

Bedford has 10.03 square miles of land and 4,977.9 residents per square mile as of 2020, and the typical trip to work is 24.5 minutes. Homes near Bedford Boys Ranch Park have an easy selling point to mention.

Homestead exemption applications go to Tarrant Appraisal District, free of charge. You can file online, send it by mail, or deliver it to the office on Handley-Ederville Road in Fort Worth.

  • Residential homestead, for owners who live in the house.
  • Over-65 and disabled exemptions, which add a ceiling on school taxes and on locally adopted city, county and special district taxes.
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, tied to the service-connected rating.
  • Heir owners can claim the homestead on the whole property rather than a share.

Owners who are 65 or older, disabled or disabled veteran owners may also put off paying the homestead tax while it keeps accruing. Someone whose value rose more than 5% over the prior year can defer the extra portion too. The deferral charges 8% interest a year, and the deferred tax stays a lien on the property.

sections.h2: How much a Bedford tax bill can grow
sections.html:
School taxes on a Texas homestead start with a $140,000 exemption, and older or disabled owners get $60,000 more. A taxing unit can add its own percentage exemption beyond that.

Assessed homestead value can rise no more than 10% a year after the first full year of exemption is behind you. Bills are sent around October 1, and unpaid balances pick up a six percent penalty plus one percent interest on February 1. A delinquent homestead owner may be allowed to pay over as many as 36 months, depending on the collector.

Yes. Before renting a home for fewer than 29 days at a time, an owner must register with the city, and no property is exempt.

Residential zoning is the only place for short-term rentals, never multi-family districts, and none may be within 1,000 feet of another registered one. Expect a fire inspection every year, a repeat visit if problems turn up, and a fresh inspection whenever ownership changes.

  • Liability insurance for the host, naming the city as an additional insured.
  • Proof that property taxes are current.
  • Written house rules on occupancy limits, off-street parking, quiet hours and a 24-hour local contact.
  • A floorplan with dimensions that shows the emergency exits.

Hotel occupancy tax is due by the 20th of each month for the month before, and a report is required even in a month with no stays. A buyer planning a rental should ask Neighborhood Services what a sale does to the registration.

sections.h2: Lender timeline on a Bedford foreclosure
sections.html:
A Tarrant County deed of trust usually gives the lender a power of sale, which means an auction with no lawsuit. Sales are held on a first Tuesday, and the posted start time may not be delayed by more than three hours.

The default notice comes first and gives you 20 days from receipt to pay what is past due. Next, the sale notice must arrive with 21 days or more to spare. A lender that wants the remaining balance after the sale must sue within two years.

sections.h2: Moving an inherited Bedford house to a buyer
sections.html:
The probate court in the decedent's home county hears the will, and you have four years from the death to start. When real estate liens are the only debts, a muniment of title allows the court order and the will to pass title.

The title company's requirements follow the route you took. Transfer on death deeds come with an affidavit of death and a certificate. Administered estates use a deed from the executor or administrator. A will with no contest and no administration is backed by the court order alone. Heirs will not be added to the old deed by the county on its own.

sections.h2: Where a Bedford deed is filed
sections.html:
A Bedford deed is filed by the Tarrant County clerk, since Texas records deeds in the county of the land. Before filing, the deed must be signed and either acknowledged by a notary or witnessed by two people.

Expect $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every page after it, plus other charges. Call the Tarrant County Clerk for the full amount before you mail in a deed.

Accepting an offer sets the title company in motion: a tax statement is requested, each payoff is ordered and the records are searched for liens. At closing you sign the deed before a notary, and it goes to the Tarrant County clerk for recording. Give the buyer the lease and deposit information if someone rents the house. This is also the time to schedule a final walk-through and plan utility shut-offs for the closing date.

sections.h2: Cash buyer or listing for a Bedford house
sections.html:
Compare what you owe with what each route is likely to bring. A listing can pay more for an updated house, yet it comes with showings, repairs after inspection and a buyer's loan to approve. Cash buyers take the house in its current state and close on your timetable, a good fit for a tenant, an estate or a deadline.

Before deciding, gather the tax statement, any mortgage payoff, rental registration and inspection records, and a copy of the deed. Then you can set offers side by side and see what each would truly leave you.

Landlords should explain the registration to every buyer. It belongs to the owner, so someone who keeps the house as a rental must register under their own name and book a new inspection after the sale.

faqs.q: What is a house in Bedford worth?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes sit at a $350,700 midpoint in the 2020-2024 figures. Your house may differ with its condition, lot and street, and a written offer or appraisal is the way to know.

faqs.q: Can I list my Bedford house on Airbnb or Vrbo?
faqs.a: You must register with the city first. Bedford asks for registration and a yearly inspection for stays shorter than 29 days, and no short-term rental can be within 1,000 feet of another.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to claim a homestead exemption in Bedford?
faqs.a: No fee applies. Tarrant Appraisal District charges nothing for exemptions, and most homestead applications are due by April 30.

faqs.q: Can a senior in Bedford postpone property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners over 65, disabled owners and disabled veteran owners may defer homestead tax. Interest accrues at 8% per year while the tax remains a lien on the house.

faqs.q: What paperwork finishes a Bedford sale?
faqs.a: A signed and acknowledged deed, filed with the Tarrant County Clerk. For an inherited house, add whichever fits: an affidavit of death, a court order or an executor's deed.
